summary: Developed an Edge AI-based real-time vision monitoring system capable of performing local AI inference on embedded devices with minimal latency. The system focused on efficient computer vision processing, real-time detection, and optimized deployment on resource-constrained hardware.

challenge.description: Traditional cloud-based AI systems introduce latency, bandwidth dependency, and scalability limitations for real-time monitoring applications. The challenge was to build a lightweight and efficient Edge AI solution capable of processing video streams locally while maintaining reliable performance.

methodology.title: Embedded System Setup
methodology.description: Configured embedded Linux environments and integrated camera modules for real-time image acquisition and processing.

methodology.title: Optimized AI Inference
methodology.description: Deployed lightweight AI models using ONNX Runtime to achieve efficient inference performance on edge hardware.

methodology.title: Real-Time Vision Pipeline
methodology.description: Implemented a low-latency computer vision pipeline for continuous monitoring, detection, and event processing.

impact.label: Latency
impact.description: Enabled fast local AI inference without reliance on cloud infrastructure.

impact.label: Frame Rate
impact.description: Supported AI execution directly on embedded and resource-constrained devices.

impact.label: Accuracy
impact.description: Optimized processing pipelines for stable operation on lightweight hardware.

impact.label: Performance
impact.description: Designed the system for integration into larger monitoring and automation environments.
